record.original_question: Is every planar graph representable by intersecting line segments using only four slopes?

evidence.quote: Question 8.4 Is every planar graph representable by intersecting line segments with four different slopes?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A segment intersection representation of a simple graph $G=(V,E)$ assigns to each vertex $v\in V$ a closed line segment $S_v$ in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ such that, for any two distinct vertices $u,v\in V$, one has $S_u\cap S_v\neq\emptyset$ if and only if $uv\in E$. The slope of a non-degenerate segment is the (unoriented) direction of the line containing it. Given a finite set $D$ of slopes, $G$ is said to be representable by segments with slopes in $D$ if there is a segment intersection representation of $G$ in which every segment has slope belonging to $D$. A graph is planar if it admits an embedding in the plane with no edge crossings.

Question: Is it true that for every planar graph $G$ there exists a set $D$ of four slopes such that $G$ admits a segment intersection representation with all segments having slopes in $D$?
artifact.status_search_result: Every planar graph is known to be an intersection graph of segments in the plane (Chalopin–Gonçalves, 2009), confirming Scheinerman's conjecture. For the four-slope refinement (West's 1991 conjecture), the PURE-4-DIR version—where parallel segments are forbidden to intersect—has been refuted: there exist planar graphs that are not in PURE-4-DIR (JGAA paper "Not all planar graphs are in PURE-4-DIR"). The unrestricted four-slope version, allowing collinear/parallel segments to intersect, does not appear to be settled in the literature found.

status_evidence.title: Not all planar graphs are in PURE-4-DIR
status_evidence.snippet: Some planar graphs are not intersection graphs of segments if only four slopes are allowed for the segments, and if parallel segments do not intersect. This refutes a conjecture of D. West.
status_evidence.claim: The PURE-4-DIR variant of West's four-slope conjecture is refuted.

status_evidence.title: Scheinerman's conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Every planar graph is the intersection graph of line segments in the plane (Chalopin and Gonçalves, 2009).
status_evidence.claim: The base Scheinerman conjecture (segment representation of planar graphs) is solved, but with no slope restriction.

status_evidence.title: 3-Colorable Planar Graphs Have an Intersection Segment Representation Using 3 Slopes
status_evidence.snippet: 3-colorable planar graphs have an intersection segment representation using 3 slopes.
status_evidence.claim: Related slope-restricted results are known for 3-colorable planar graphs.
